properties.name: cargo's missing GC filled the disk to 100%: 263 GiB in 484,912 artifacts, almost all duplicate copies of reflow2's OWN two crates — and the surgical sweep keeps RocksDB cached
properties.statement:
MEASURED 2026-08-24, when a `cargo test --workspace` failed with `No space left on device (os error 28)` and Anthony's desktop reported 756.8 MB free. It arrived sideways — nobody was looking at disk; increment 2 of the foundation absorption was being verified.

═══ WHAT WAS THERE ═══

    filesystem            468 G total, 428 G used, 17 G free (97%)  — briefly 43 MB
    target/debug          267 G
      └ deps             263 G across 472,078 artifacts
      └ incremental       22 G
    reflow2_core|reflow2_mcp artifacts       159,247
    ONE reflow2_mcp test binary                 290 MB
    liblibrocksdb_sys.rlib                      856 MB  (the single largest dep)

⇒ **THE BULK IS NOT DEPENDENCIES. IT IS THIS PROJECT'S OWN TWO CRATES, over and over.** Every `cargo test --workspace` mints another generation of ~290 MB test binaries and nothing ever removes the previous one. Four workspace runs in one session is a meaningful fraction of a terabyte.

═══ ⭐ THE SWEEP, AND WHICH COMMAND MATTERS ═══

    cargo clean -p reflow2-core -p reflow2-mcp
    → Removed 484,912 files, 263.1 GiB
    → target/debug 267 G → 6.1 G ; disk 97% → 38% used, 277 G free
    → liblibrocksdb_sys.rlib STILL CACHED (896,538,384 bytes, verified after)

🛑 **THE `-p` FLAGS ARE THE WHOLE POINT.** A bare `cargo clean` reclaims the same space and ALSO destroys the cached RocksDB C++ build — a ~19-minute rebuild bought for nothing, since the 263 GiB is not RocksDB. Scoped to the two crates, only reflow2's own code recompiles, which was going to happen anyway. `rm -rf target/debug/incremental` is the free first move: pure cache, always safe, 22 GB here.

═══ IT WAS ALREADY DIAGNOSED, AND HAD GROWN ~87× SINCE ═══

`[profile.dev]` in the workspace Cargo.toml already carries the finding: *"cargo has no GC. target/debug/deps held 1,824 artifacts under 104 distinct names (43 copies of the reflow2_mcp test binary alone); sweeping the stale duplicates recovered 225 GiB. Sweep first when the disk is tight; these settings only slow the refill."*

That comment is still true and is NOT superseded — it describes an earlier sweep. What is new: **1,824 artifacts became 159,247 for these two crates**, and the comment says WHAT happened without naming the command that does it safely. That gap is what cost this session a failed test run.

⚠️ NOT MEASURED, so the number is not read wider than it is: how fast it refills per workspace run. Four runs happened between the previous healthy state and the wall, but nothing sampled the growth in between, so "a few runs fills a disk" is an inference from two endpoints rather than a rate.

═══ WHERE THIS BEARS ON AN OPEN QUESTION ═══

`dec:idea-a-byte-backend-that-compiles-in-seconds` records that RocksDB's DISK cost is uncontested even though its COMPILE cost turned out not to be what made this session slow (measured: zero RocksDB recompiles across three long builds). This measurement sharpens both halves — RocksDB's 856 MB artifact is real but is 0.3% of what actually filled the disk. **A backend swap would not have prevented this.**
